headline: High: Airbyte can exfiltrate business data over broad egress while Argo Workflows can move artifacts/parameters through shared pipelines, creating default data-leak and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented, but Airbyte can emit data over broad network egress and Argo Workflows consumes artifacts/parameters via APIs, so a manual or pipeline bridge could carry malicious content. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not directly evidenced, so I choose low rather than none.
conditions: IF Airbyte outputs are copied into an Argo artifact or parameter without sanitization
IF an operator uses a shared filesystem or message bridge between Airbyte and Argo
mitigations: Restrict the bridge to typed parameters only
Add content sanitization before Argo ingestion
Use separate workspaces for each agent
Review any copied payloads before execution

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; Argo Workflows touches artifacts and parameters and can call REST/GRPC APIs. In a default pipeline, shared artifacts can leak business data into workflow outputs or remote services. The interaction is inferred from profiles, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF business data is passed from Airbyte into Argo artifacts or parameters
IF Argo workflow steps forward those artifacts to external services
mitigations: Minimize fields exported from Airbyte
Encrypt or redact artifacts before Argo ingestion
Disable unnecessary outbound destinations in Argo
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive pipelines
Audit workflow outputs for business data

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents expose API surfaces and can move data, but neither profile shows unrestricted filesystem write, git mutation, or overlapping OAuth scopes. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; only limited coordination conflict is plausible, so low fits.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same mutable external resource
IF an orchestrator maps both agents onto one shared state store
mitigations: Assign separate resource namespaces
Add locking around shared writes
Avoid concurrent writes to the same dataset
Use idempotent operations where possible

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte produces business data that Argo Workflows can consume as artifacts or parameters. If Argo treats those inputs as authoritative, a bad extraction or malformed payload can cascade into downstream workflow actions. No verification step is documented, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Argo consumes Airbyte output without validation
IF downstream workflow steps act on those values automatically
mitigations: Validate schema before workflow execution
Insert a human approval gate for critical steps
Add checksum or provenance checks
Fail closed on malformed inputs

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only business data/artifacts/parameters are listed, with no explicit residency, HIPAA, or GDPR mismatch. A compliance issue is possible if regulated data is introduced, but the profiles do not document such a mismatch, so low is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is routed through either agent
IF deployment policies require residency or retention controls not configured here
mitigations: Classify data before routing
Apply retention limits to workflow logs
Keep regulated datasets out of the pair
Document residency and deletion handling
